2027 Application Guide: Doctoral Program in Medicine
Graduate School of Medicine, the University of Tokyo
This application guide may change. The University of Tokyo website (https://www.m.u-
tokyo.ac.jp/english/daigakuin/apply/appguidemain.html) will continuously announce if there is
any change, so please check the newest information constantly.
Purpose of Education for Research
The purpose of research training in the Graduate School of Medicine is to promote advanced research that
will contribute to breakthroughs in the understanding of the mechanisms of life, to improve health, to contribute
to the struggle against disease, and to foster international leaders in all fields of medicine who are outstanding
scholars and highly creative researchers.
Admission Policy
Consistent with the aims described above, for its PhD programs in the Graduate School of Medicine, the
University of Tokyo seeks students who have the potential to become international leaders in all fields of
medicine through outstanding scholarship and advanced and highly creative research. We seek those who
will, as described above, contribute to the understanding of the mechanisms of life, to preventing, curing, and
recovering from disease, and to promoting and supporting healthy human development.
1. Eligibility criteria
(1) Persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from a program to study medicine or dentistry
at a Japanese university by 31 March 2027. (Note 1)
(2) Persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from a six-year program to study pharmacy
or veterinary medicine at a Japanese university by 31 March 2027. (Note 1)
(3) Persons who have completed or are expected to complete 18 years of overseas curricular education
(ending with a program in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or veterinary medicine) by 31 March 2027.
(Note 2)
Nota bene: Persons on whom a foreign university has not conferred (and is not expected to confer)
a Bachelor's degree in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, or veterinary medicine provided they meet
the conditions related to the restrictions described in (7) or (8) below, and after undergoing individual
eligibility review to determine whether their academic ability is equivalent or superior to that of
graduates of a program of study in medicine, etc., at a Japanese university, may be granted eligibility
to take the entrance examination -- provided that, before applying, they have undergone the
[individual] eligibility review whose application procedure requirements are described in Note 6 and
Note 7 below.
(4) Persons who have been conferred or are expected to be conferred a degree equivalent to that of a
bachelor's degree from a foreign university or other foreign institution of higher education (restricted to
those whose comprehensive status of education and research activities has been assessed by the
government of the said foreign country or a related organization) by March 31, 2027, having completed
a program (restricted to a program to study veterinary medicine, medicine, pharmacy or dentistry) which
requires at least five years of study. (Note 2)
Nota bene: Persons on whom degrees have been conferred (or are expected to be conferred) by a
foreign university with a five-year program of study and whose final program of study is neither
medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, nor veterinary medicine, are not eligible to apply under the conditions
1
described here. This notwithstanding however, provided they meet the conditions related to such
restrictions described in (7) or (8) below, after undergoing individual eligibility review to determine
whether their academic ability is equivalent or superior to that of graduates of a program of study in
medicine, etc., at a Japanese university, may be granted eligibility to take the entrance examination -
- provided that, before applying, they have undergone the [individual] eligibility review whose
application procedure requirements are described in Note 6 and Note 7 below.
(5) Persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from an educational institution designated by
the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology by March 31, 2027. (Note 3)
(6) Persons who have graduated from a master’s program, etc. (Note 4) at a Japanese university and are
recognized by the Graduate School of Medicine based on an eligibility review as having academic
ability equivalent to or surpassing that of a person who has graduated from a program in medicine,
etc. (Note 5) at a Japanese university. (Note 1)
(7) Persons who have engaged or are expected in research for 2 years or more at a university or a research
institute by March 31, 2027 after graduating from a Japanese university (excluding programs in medicine,
dentistry, or pharmacy or veterinary medicine) or completing 16 years of overseas curricular education
and are recognized by the Graduate School of Medicine based on an eligibility review as having
academic ability equivalent to or surpassing that of a person who has completed a program in medicine,
etc. (Note 5) at a Japanese university. (Note 1) (Note 6)
Nota bene: This clause pertains to persons with documented evidence of two or more years'
employment doing research at a university or a research institute etc.
(8) Persons who are recognized by the Graduate School of Medicine based on an individual eligibility review
as having academic ability equivalent to or surpassing that of a Japanese university graduate, and who
are aged 24 years or older on 31 March 2027. (Note 7)
Nota bene: This clause pertains to persons on whom a Master's degree has been conferred by a foreign
university; note that, before applying for admission, applicants must undergo an individual eligibility
review (Note 7).
Note also that applicants' Bachelor's degree may have been conferred irrespectively either by a
Japanese or by a foreign university.
Nota bene: Clause (7) above, not this clause, pertains to persons with documented evidence of two or
more years' employment doing research at a university or a research institute etc.
Note 1:”Japanese university” mentioned in Eligibilities (1), (2), (6) (7), and (8) above is a university within the boundaries
of Japan and as prescribed in Article 83 of the School Education Law.
Note 2: Eligibilities (3) and (4) above include the case of having completed a distance education program provided by a
foreign school of said country while residing in Japan.
Note 3: “Persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from an educational institution designated by the
Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology” as per eligibility criterion (5) are as follows:
① Persons who have studied medicine or dentistry at the medical or dentistry faculty of a university prescribed
by the old University Ordinance and who have graduated from either of these faculties.
② Persons who have graduated from the National Defense Medical College under the Act for Establishment of
the Ministry of Defense.
③ Persons who have completed a program of a foreign university (restricted to those who have competed 18
years of bachelor’s education in the school education system of said foreign country, ending with a program
either in veterinary medicine, medicine, pharmacy or dentistry) while in Japan, the said program having been
designated separately by the Minister for Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology and belonging
to an educational institution under the school education system of the said foreign country.
2
Note 4: “Persons who have completed a master’s program, etc. at a Japanese university” as per eligibility criterion (6)
are as follows:
① Persons who have completed a master's program or a professional degree program at a Japanese university
and those who are eligible to be conferred a master's degree.
② Persons who have been enrolled for at least two years in a doctoral program which is not separated into
former and latter parts, and have obtained at least 30 academic credits in addition to the required research
guidance at a Japanese university.
Nota bene: Applicants are considered eligible if either ① or ② above pertain; prior review of their entrance
examination eligibility is not required.
Note 5: ”A program in medicine, etc. at a Japanese university” mentioned in Eligibility (6), (7) and (8) above is an
undergraduate program at a Japanese university as follows:
① A program to study medicine
② A program to study dentistry
③ A program to study pharmacy whose main purpose is to cultivate practical clinical ability
④ A program to study veterinary medicine
Note 6: Persons who intend to apply for admission under eligibility criteria (7) above must first undergo an eligibility
review. To undergo the eligibility review, it is necessary for applicants to contact the Administration Office (refer
to 6(4) below) in advance and to submit the required documents to the Office by Thursday, 11 June, 2026.
Persons who are deemed by the Graduate School of Medicine on the basis of an eligibility review to have
academic ability equivalent or superior to that of a university graduate described in eligibility criteria (1) or (2)
shall be permitted to take the entrance exam upon application.
Eligibility review result will be notified by Email around late June, 2026.
Note 7:  Eligibility criterion (8) above is intended for those who do not fall under eligibility criteria (1) - (7) and have
graduated from/completed a program to study medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or veterinary medicine at an
educational institution that is equivalent to a six-year university, and have been deemed by the Graduate School
of Medicine on the basis of an individual eligibility review to have academic ability equivalent or superior to that
of a university graduate described in eligibility criteria (1) or (2).
Persons who intend to apply for admission under eligibility criterion (8) above must first undergo an individual
eligibility review. To undergo the individual eligibility review, it is necessary for applicants to contact the
Administration Office (refer to 6(4) below) in advance and to submit the required documents to the Office by
Thursday, 11 June, 2026.
 Persons who are deemed by the Graduate School of Medicine on the basis of an individual eligibility review to
have academic ability equivalent or superior to that of a university graduate described in eligibility criteria (1) or
(2), shall be permitted to take the entrance exam upon application.
Eligibility review result will be notified by Email around late June, 2026.

Admission shall be determined based on a comprehensive judgement of the academic
performance of the school they came from, the results of other documents screening, written
examination and oral exam and so on.

6. Application procedure
(1) ・Applicants must contact faculty member before applying.
・Applicants must declare at the time of application if they have a familial relationship (within two
degrees of kinship, including cohabitation or shared livelihood) with a faculty member in the intended
field of specialization, including the prospective supervisor, or if they are currently employed full-time
and their employer has a conflict of interest (COI) with the intended field.
Such declarations will not be used for admission selection and will be used only to ensure fairness
and for COI management after enrollment.
If any such relationship arises after application, it must be reported promptly to the Administration
Office (refer to 6(4) below).
(2) Applications must be submitted online. For details, please refer to the Graduate School’s website.
(URL: https://www.m.u-tokyo.ac.jp/daigakuin/apply/appguidemain.html)

2026 must first contact the Administration Office (see 6(4) below for contact details).

10
7. Other important points
(1) The examination card will be issued in early July 2026 via your My Page on the Web Application System;
please print it out and bring it with you on the day of the examination. The "Notes on the Examination"
will be sent separately to the email address provided in your application. If you cannot confirm these
by mid-September, contact our office (indicated in section 6.(4)) for instructions.
(2) If you select a written exam subject other than that specified for your desired major, the exam will be
invalid.
(3) Following the submission of application documents, changes to the documents or the refund of exam
fees will not be allowed under any circumstances. Once application documents are received, they are
not returnable.
(4) Those who wish to maintain their employment at a government office, school, hospital, or private
company during enrollment are required to submit a consent form (format optional) from their employer
when completing the admission procedures (see 5(3) above), to the effect that they will remain
committed to their studies while enrolled.
(5) International students are required to obtain the appropriate visa according to the Immigration Control
and Refugee Recognition Act (Cabinet Order No. 319 of 1951) prior to undertaking the admission
procedures.
(6) Admission fees shall not be refunded under any circumstances following the completion of admission
procedures.
(7) The University of Tokyo provides reasonable accommodations to ensure that individuals with disabilities
are not disadvantaged during entrance examinations and studies after enrollment, and provides
consultations for this purpose. Those who wish to request accommodations for entrance examinations
should contact the administrative office indicated in section 6.(4) by 11 June, 2026. Although requests
made after the above deadline will still be considered, it is recommended that applicants send their
requests well in advance as it may not be possible to provide certain accommodations without sufficient
preparation time. (Please refer to the following website for more details: https://www.m.u-
tokyo.ac.jp/daigakuin/apply/appguidemain.html )
(8) Names, addresses, or other personal information obtained from applications will only be used for: 
screening of applicants (application processing & screening);  the announcement of successful
applicants; and  tasks related to admission procedures. This personal information will also be used
for:  academic affairs (enrollment records, learning etc.);  student support (health management,
employment assistance, applications for scholarships and exemption from tuition fees, use of libraries,
etc.); and  collection of tuition fees.
(9) If any false statement or forgery in the application documents, or if there is clear evidence that there
was any fraudulent activity during the examination, that student’s admittance may be canceled even
after enrolling in or going on to a graduate school.
(10) The examination results used in the selection of entrants may be used in future studies for the
improvement of both the entrance examination and the education at the University of Tokyo.
(11) The University of Tokyo has established the “The University of Tokyo Security Export Control
Regulations” in accordance with Japan’s “Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act”, and rigorously
implements security export control for potential students before and after their enrollment on the basis
of these regulations. In particular, pre-enrollment screenings are mandatory for all international
students and also for Japanese students in certain circumstances.
Please be aware that applicants who fall under any of the conditions set out in the Act may not receive
permission to enroll at the university or may have their research activities restricted after their
enrollment even if they have passed the entrance examinations.
May 2026

=== https://www.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/hubfs/admission/2026/0403/me_guide_e_2.pdf (status=200, chars=15944, file=66cdb1516ec4931b.json) ===
This document is a translation of the authoritative Japanese version.
Entrance Examination Guide for the 2027 Academic Year,
Department of Mechanical Engineering,
Graduate School of Engineering,
The University of Tokyo
Master’s Program (Application Schedule A)
Doctoral Program (Application Schedules A and B)
･In case that the contents of this entrance examination guide should change, the revised
guide will be published on the websites of the School of Engineering;
(https://www.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/study-at-utokyo/soe/apply)
and the Department of Mechanical Engineering;
(https://www2.mech.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/admissions/?lang=en). Please confirm these websites as
needed.
Inquiries about this guide:
7-3-1 Hongo, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo 113-8656
Department of Mechanical Engineering Administrative Office, Graduate School of
Engineering, The University of Tokyo
Tel: 03-5841-6301
Email: kyoumu@office.mech.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp
This guide serves as a supplement to the “Guidelines for Applicants to the 2027 Master's
Program of the Graduate School of Engineering, The University of Tokyo” and the “Guidelines
for Applicants to the 2027 Doctoral Program of the Graduate School of Engineering, The
University of Tokyo.” Applicants must read this guide along with the aforementioned
application guidelines.
1. Admission Schedule
(Application Schedule A)
・For the master’s program, the qualified applicants who are expected to graduate from a
university by March 31, 2027, will be enrolled in April 2027, and the qualified applicants
who are already graduated from a university at the time they apply or expected to
graduate by September 30, 2026, may be enrolled in either October 2026 or April 2027.
・For the doctoral program, the qualified applicants who are expected to complete a
graduate school master’s program by March 31, 2027, will be enrolled in April 2027, and
the qualified applicants who already completed a graduate school master’s program or are
expected to complete it by September 30, 2026, may be enrolled in either October 2026 or
April 2027.
(Application Schedule B)
･Applicants for the Application Schedule B examination will only be enrolled in April 2027.
2. Supervisors
Faculty members indicated by a diamond (◇) in the faculty list cannot serve as supervisors
for students in any program. Faculty members indicated by a double circle (◎) cannot serve
as supervisors for students in the doctoral program.
Note: The faculty list is accurate as of April 2026 and is subject to change.
(1) Master’s program
The applicants to the master’s program who choose the special oral selection in “3.
Master’s Program” must fill out the inquiry sheet and submit it when submitting the
application form. The applicants who do not choose the special oral selection must fill out
the inquiry sheet, which will be sent with the examination admission card, and submit it
by the indicated deadline. The choice of supervisor will be based on the results of the
examination and the requests from all the applicants, thus the choice of supervisor will
not necessarily be the same as the first choice of an applicant. Please read the instructions
on the inquiry sheet carefully and fill in the names of faculty members whom you wish to
be your supervisor.
(2) Doctoral program
The applicants to the doctoral program must first receive consent from a prospective
supervisor and discuss issues including their research topics before submitting their
applications. The applicants are requested to submit the specified confirmation note
issued by their prospective supervisors with their applications. It is also possible to consult
with the Department Chair regarding the selection of supervisors.
Department Chair: Professor Gentiane VENTURE Tel: +81-3-5841-6355
3. Master’s Program (Application Schedule A only)
In the entrance examination for the 2027 academic year (held in 2026), the "Special Oral
Selection" is introduced for applicants who wish to enroll in the Master's Program in the
Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Graduate School of Engineering, The
University of Tokyo.
Applicants who choose the special oral selection when submitting the application form will
be screened (document screening) and will take a special oral examination in July 2026. For
those who are selected by the special oral selection, supervisors will be assigned and the
written examination will be exempted (the interview test will not be exempted). Those who
are not selected by the special oral selection will automatically become eligible for the
written examination (regular admission) to be held from late August to early September
2026.
Those who do not choose the special oral selection at the time of application will be eligible
for the regular admission.
(1) Special oral selection
For information on the special oral selection and forms for submission, refer to the
Department of Mechanical Engineering website
(https://www.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/soe/admission/general-guideline).
(a) Document screening
In late June, applicants who choose the special oral selection are screened by the
following documents i) through vi), which are submitted to the Department of
Mechanical Engineering at the time of application from late May to early June 2026.
The result will be notified promptly after the completion of the document screening.
i) Special oral selection Form A for the Department of Mechanical Engineering
ii) Transcripts
Prospective graduates must submit transcripts showing grades from the first to
third year of university. However, prospective graduates of the two mechanical
engineering departments of The University of Tokyo (Department of Mechanical
Engineering and Department of Mechano-Informatics) are not required to submit
these documents (those who have already graduated from the two mechanical
engineering departments of The University of Tokyo are required to submit these
documents).
iii) Documents showing the number of credits for graduation up to the 4th year of
university (may be omitted if the transcript shows this information) (not required
for graduates).
iv) Special oral selection Form B (inquiry sheet) for the Department of Mechanical
Engineering.
v) Special oral selection Form C for the Department of Mechanical Engineering.
vi) Official English score (TOEFL-iBT or TOEFL-iBT Home Edition *).
(b) Special oral examination
Only applicants who pass document screening will be allowed to take the special oral
examination online by late July.
The results of the special oral selection will be notified promptly after the special oral
examination. Selected applicants will also be notified of the supervisor to be assigned.
Applicants who are not selected by the special oral selection will automatically be
eligible for the written examination from late August to early September 2026.
(2) Regular admission
(a) Written examination
The written examination for the Master’s Program covers a) general education subject
(mathematics), b) foreign language (please submit your TOEFL score*), and c) the
following specialized subjects (mechanical engineering).
Specialized Subject Fields
Mechanical Questions are primarily from the fields of thermal engineering and
engineering (part 1) fluid engineering.
Questions are primarily from the fields of material mechanics,
Mechanical
mechanical dynamics/control engineering and mechanical
engineering (part 2)
design/production engineering.
International students and examinees will be provided with an English version of the
exam questions for the specialized subject (mechanical engineering) upon request. An
English version of the exam questions for the general education subject (mathematics)
will be provided. For the examination in mathematics, select and answer three out of
six questions.
(b) Interview test
The interview test will only be held for candidates selected through the special oral
examination and for those who have passed the written examination, the results of
which will be announced at 12:30 p.m. on September 4 (Friday). The candidates will be
asked questions about their desired specialized field, research topics, supervisor choice,
as well as other subjects. The candidate will be called in the order that is announced at
the designated meeting place on the examination day. Please note that the candidates
who are not present when called will be disqualified from the interview test.
Note that even those who have been selected by the special oral selection and are
exempted from the written examination will ultimately fail the interview test if they
are absent.
(3) Application schedule
Please see the “Guidelines for Applicants to the 2027 Master's Program Graduate School
of Engineering, The University of Tokyo.”
4. Doctoral Program
(1) Primary examination
(a) Written examination
The written examination in the primary examination for the doctoral program covers a)
foreign language (English TOEFL score* must be submitted) and b) the specialized
contents for the doctoral program (the contents related to each examinee’s specialized
field). However, candidates who have completed or are expected to complete a master’s
degree at the Graduate School of Engineering, The University of Tokyo, are exempted
from a) the foreign language examination and only need to take the b) the specialized
contents for the doctoral program (the contents related to each examinee’s the
specialized field).
Both Japanese and English versions of the exam questions for the doctoral program
specialized content examination (content related to your specialized field) will be
provided.
(b) Oral examination
The examination includes questions about a) one of the academic fields in the
specialized subject (mechanical engineering) that is stated in the specified confirmation
note issued by your prospective supervisor, b) the progress on your master’s thesis or
equivalent research and the research plans of the subject you wish to address, as well
as your knowledge of mechanical engineering related to your research. However,
applicants who have completed or are expected to complete a master’s degree at the
Department of Mechanical Engineering in the Graduate School of Engineering, The
University of Tokyo, are exempted from taking the examination part a) related to the
specialized subject (mechanical engineering).
(2) Secondary examination
Only the applicants who have passed the primary examination will be allowed to take the
secondary examination for the doctoral program. The secondary examination consists of a
presentation and a Q&A session on your completed master’s thesis or other equivalent
research.
As a rule, the examination is held from late January to early February for applicants of
Application Schedules A and B. However, for the applicants of Application Schedule A who
have already completed a graduate school master’s program or are expected to complete
it by September 30, 2026, the secondary examination will be held in early September.
Details will be notified in due course.
(3) About the application schedule
Please see the “Guidelines for Applicants to the 2027 Doctoral Program Graduate School
of Engineering, The University of Tokyo.”
5. Miscellaneous
・The written examination and oral examination will be held at the Hongo Campus, The
University of Tokyo.
* Applicants must have taken the TOEFL (iBT or iBT Home Edition) and submitted their
official score. Submission deadlines are June 4 for the master’s program applicants who
choose the special oral selection and August 6 for the master’s program applicants who do
not choose the special oral selection and doctoral program applicants. The TOEFL-ITP test
is not administered at the graduate school entrance examination center. The applicants of
the Application Schedule A failing to submit their official TOEFL score must report to the
department office by May 29. Please see the attached guidelines “AY 2027 Graduate School
of Engineering Entrance Examinations Guidelines for Submission of TOEFL Scores” for
more details. As for the TOEFL-iBT, the Department of Mechanical Engineering uses the
Test Date score as your submitted score and disregards the MyBestTM score.
* It is recommended that the masterʼs program applicants who do not choose the special oral
selection also submit TOEFL scores by June 4.

=== https://www.i.u-tokyo.ac.jp/edu/entra/2027_ag_d_e.pdf (status=200, chars=32389, file=672483114ade97f4.json) ===
The document is a translation from the official Japanese version.

AY2027 Admission Guide: Doctoral Program
Graduate School of Information Science and Technology
The University of Tokyo
Examinations Conducted in AY2026
*In the event that the contents of this Admission Guide are revised, the latest information is to be posted on the
admission webpage of this graduate school (https://www.i.u-tokyo.ac.jp/edu/entra/entra_e.shtml). Applicants
should periodically check the webpage.
Education and Research Goals
The education and research goals at this graduate school are to provide an environment where students can
master their systematic knowledge of information science and technology, and to foster individuals who will
act as leaders in research and development through the pursuit of the scientific method, thereby contributing to
the further development of this field.
Prospective Students
Those with deep insight into information science and technology, who have the necessary abilities for
international activities, and who possess strong motivation and talent for pioneering uncharted fields to create
the future.
Admission Policy
1. The doctoral program of the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology, the University of
Tokyo, seeks students who have sufficient technical knowledge of specialized topics and have a strong desire
to contribute to society through research in their specialized fields. Students are expected to develop a
distinguished expanse of knowledge in the field of information science and technology.
2. During the screening process, we will evaluate comprehensively if applicants meet the following conditions,
through submitted documents, written examinations, oral examinations, etc.:
(a) Applicants have a deep knowledge of the specialized topics they wish to study and have the ability to
contribute to the development of academic fields through research on information science and technology.
(b) Applicants can set their own advanced research goals based on the needs of society and achieve those goals
by utilizing fundamental knowledge of information science and technology.
(c) Applicants have enough language capabilities to compete on a global stage and credentials to contribute to
the improvement of future society.
1. Entrance Examinations and Entrance Date
Examinations are held twice a year, Summer Entrance Examinations and Winter Entrance Examinations, in
each department: Computer Science; Mathematical Informatics; Information Physics and Computing;
1
The document is a translation from the official Japanese version.
In the case of conflict, the Japanese version shall prevail and be conclusive.
Information and Communication Engineering; Mechano-Informatics; and Creative Informatics.
The entrance dates for successful applicants for the Summer Entrance Examinations and for the Winter Entrance
Examinations are in April 2027 and October 2027 respectively (hereafter referred to as “Standard Entrance
Dates”). Some departments may allow October 2026 entry for successful applicants for the Summer Entrance
Examinations and may allow April 2027 entry for successful applicants for the Winter Entrance Examinations
(hereafter referred to as “Early Entrance”) if applicants indicate this preference on the application form. If
applicants are required to newly apply for a Certificate of Eligibility for a Status of Residence (COE) to enter
the University of Tokyo, the Standard Entrance Dates are highly recommended.* The Standard Entrance Dates
are also recommended for other applicants, as a Letter of Acceptance for Admission may be issued later than
the time specified in Section 8 below due to screening by The University of Tokyo Security Export Control, etc.
*As described in 10. Important Notes (6), applicants with foreign nationalities must obtain a visa permitting enrollment at
a Japanese graduate school by the time of enrollment procedures. Since obtaining a new visa normally takes approximately
three months after the admission notification for successful applicants, a visa cannot be obtained in time for Early Entrance.
Regarding the details on the procedure from announcement of the examination result to enrollment, refer to the
accompanying document “Timeline of Enrollment Procedures for New International Students”.
2. Requirements for Eligibility
The eligibility requirements for applicants desiring April 2027 entry are as follows. If desiring October 2026
entry, replace “March 31, 2027” below with “September 30, 2026”, and if desiring October 2027 entry, replace
“March 31, 2027” with “September 30, 2027”.
(1) Those who have obtained, or are expected to obtain by March 31, 2027, a Master’s or Professional degree
at a Japanese university.*1
(2) Those who have obtained or are expected to obtain a Master’s degree by March 31, 2027, from the National
Institution for Academic Degrees and Quality Enhancement of Higher Education (NIAD-QE).
(3) Those who have obtained, or are expected to obtain by March 31, 2027, a degree equivalent to a Master’s
or Professional degree in a foreign country.*2
(4) Those who have completed, or are expected to complete a program at an educational institution in Japan that
is part of the school education system of a foreign country and has a graduate school program of that foreign
country, and that is designated so by the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology,
and consequently have obtained or are expected to obtain by March 31, 2027, a degree equivalent to a
Master’s or Professional degree.
(5) Those who have completed or are expected to complete a program at the United Nations University and
have obtained or are expected to obtain a degree equivalent to a Master’s degree by March 31, 2027.
(6) Those who have passed or are expected to pass by March 31, 2027, a screening for the fundamental ability
for doctorate dissertation research as specified in Article 16-2 of the Standards for Establishment of Graduate
Schools at a school abroad, an educational institution mentioned in Requirement (4) above, or the United
Nations University, and are recognized by this graduate school as having academic abilities at least
equivalent to a holder of a Master's degree.*3
2
The document is a translation from the official Japanese version.
In the case of conflict, the Japanese version shall prevail and be conclusive.
(7) Those who have graduated from a Japanese university or have completed at least 16 years of academic
education overseas, and have been engaged in research at a university, research institute or other institution
in Japan or abroad for at least 2 years, or are expected to have been engaged in research for at least 2 years
by March 31, 2027, and are recognized by this graduate school as having academic abilities at least
equivalent to a holder of a Master’s or Professional degree as a result of the research.*1*2*3
(8) Those aged twenty-four (24) years or older as of March 31, 2027, whom the Graduate School of Information
Science and Technology recognizes as having academic abilities at least equivalent to a holder of a Master’s
or Professional degree, based on individual screening of entrance qualification.*4
*1 Japanese universities mentioned in Requirements (1) and (7) above are universities within the boundaries of Japan and
as prescribed in Article 83 of the School Education Law.
*2 Requirements (3) and (7) above include the case of having completed a correspondence program provided by a foreign
school of said country while residing in Japan.
*3 1) Those who wish to apply based on Requirements (6) or (7) above must submit the documents designated by the
Graduate School of Information Science and Technology to the Admissions Office (ref. Section 11 below) by
Wednesday, May 13, 2026, in the case of Summer Entrance Examinations, and by Monday, October 26, 2026, in the
case of Winter Entrance Examinations, as the eligibility for application is confirmed individually in advance by
document screening. Applicants should inquire in advance at the Graduate School of Information Science and
Technology Admissions Office for information about documents to be submitted.
2) Those who are recognized as having academic abilities that are at least equivalent to a holder of a Master’s or
Professional degree through screening of entrance qualifications will be permitted to apply for and take the entrance
examination.
*4 1) Those covered under Requirement (8) above are those who are not covered under (1) through (7) above and whom
this graduate school has recognized, through individual screening of entrance qualifications, as having academic
abilities at least equivalent to a holder of a Master’s or Professional degree.
2) Those who wish to apply based on Requirement (8) above must submit the documents designated by the Graduate
School of Information Science and Technology to the Admissions Office (ref. Section 11 below) by Wednesday, May
13, 2026, in the case of Summer Entrance Examinations, and by Monday, October 26, 2026, in the case of Winter
Entrance Examinations, as the eligibility for application is confirmed individually in advance by document screening.
Applicants should inquire in advance at the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology Admissions
Office regarding the documents to be submitted.
3) Those who are recognized, through screening of entrance qualification, as having academic abilities at least
equivalent to a holder of a Master's or Professional degree will be permitted to apply for and take the entrance
examination.
3. Screening Process
Screening of the successful applicants for admission will be conducted by comprehensively taking into account
the results of the written examination, oral examination, submitted documents, and the applicant's Master's
thesis or its alternative.
(Note 1) The details of the screening process may differ for each department. Please refer to the Admission Guide for the
applicable department for detailed information.
(Note 2) As professional applicants may be eligible to apply for a Doctoral Program [Special Selection for Professionals],
they should also obtain the Admission Guide of Doctoral Program [Special Selection for Professionals] and refer
to the Admission Guide for the applicable department for detailed information.

8. Admission Notification and Enrollment Procedures
(1) Summer Entrance Examinations
1. The list of the successful applicants will be posted on the website of the Graduate School of Information
Science and Technology (https://www.i.u-tokyo.ac.jp/index_e.shtml the same hereafter) at approximately
15:00 on Wednesday, September 9, 2026.
2. The Letter of Acceptance for Admission for entry in October 2026 will be delivered via E-mail around early
September 2026 (TBD) after the screening for “The University of Tokyo Security Export Control” is
completed. The Letter of Acceptance for Admission for entry in April 2027 will be delivered via E-mail by
late October 2026 (TBD), after the screening for “The University of Tokyo Security Export Control” is
completed.
(2) Winter Entrance Examinations
1. The list of successful applicants will be posted on the website of the Graduate School of Information Science
and Technology at approximately 15:00 on Monday, February 15, 2027.
2. The Letter of Acceptance for Admission for entry in April 2027 will be delivered via E-mail around late
February 2027 (TBD) after the screening for “The University of Tokyo Security Export Control” is
completed. The Letter of Acceptance for Admission for entry in October 2027 will be delivered via E-mail
by late March 2027 (TBD), after the screening for “The University of Tokyo Security Export Control” is
completed.
(3) Applicants who have received the Letter of Acceptance for Admission should follow the required enrollment
procedures (i.e., payment of admission fee and submission of enrollment documents) by following the
instructions delivered separately. For entry in October 2026, these procedures must be completed by
Thursday, September 24, 2026 (TBD); for entry in April 2027, these procedures must be completed by
Thursday, March 11, 2027 (TBD); and for entry in October 2027, these procedures must be completed by
Wednesday, September 22, 2027 (TBD). Failure to complete the enrollment procedures by the designated
date will be considered cancellation of admission. The instructions for enrollment procedures will be
delivered via E-mail by early September 2026 for entry in October 2026, by late February 2027 for entry in
April 2027, and by early September for entry in October 2027.
(4) Admission Fee and Tuition (estimated amounts for AY2027)
1. Admission fee: 282,000 yen
2. Tuition for half-year: 260,400 yen (Annual amount: 520,800 yen)
(Note1) The fees indicated above are estimates. If the amounts are amended by the time of admission or during
enrollment, the new amounts will apply from the time of the amendment.
(Note2) These fees are waived for international students on the Japanese government (MEXT) scholarships.
(Note3) The admission fee will not be charged to those who complete a Master’s program or professional degree program
at our university immediately before the desired enrollment date (in September for those enrolling in October,

10. Important Notes
(1) Applicants may not apply to more than one department, program, or selection scheme at the same time for
each of the Summer and Winter Entrance Examinations.
In addition, applicants who have already passed the Summer Entrance Examinations for the Graduate
School of Information Science and Technology cannot apply for the Winter Entrance Examinations without
first declining the enrollment. Similarly, applicants who have already passed the Winter Entrance
Examinations of the Graduate School of the Information Science and Technology in the previous academic
year, cannot apply for the Summer Entrance Examinations without first declining the enrollment.
(2) Applicants cannot be enrolled in the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology while also
enrolled in other universities (as prescribed in the School Education Law) or other schools at the University
of Tokyo.
(3) Applications will not be accepted if the documents specified in Section 7 above are not submitted in full
by the application deadline. Regarding TOEFL Score submissions, follow the “Guidelines for Submission
of TOEFL Scores (for AY2027 Entrance Examinations), Graduate School of Information Science and
Technology, the University of Tokyo”. After the application process is completed, no changes to the
documents will be accepted and there will be no refund of the examination fee, under any circumstances.
(4) Examination Admission Card is delivered via E-mail to each applicant.
1. For Summer Entrance Examinations, if the Examination Admission Card is not delivered by 17:00 on
Friday, July 17, 2026, contact the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology Admissions
Office (ref. Section 11 below) for instructions on taking the examination. Do not inquire about the arrival
status of the Examination Admission Card before 17:00 on Friday, July 17, 2026.
2. For Winter Entrance Examinations, if the Examination Admission Card is not delivered by 17:00 on
Thursday, December 17, 2026, contact the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology
Admissions Office (ref. Section 11 below) for instructions on taking the examination. Do not inquire about
the arrival status of the Examination Admission Card before 17:00 on Thursday, December 17, 2026.
(5) The University of Tokyo provides reasonable accommodations to ensure that individuals with disabilities,
etc. are not disadvantaged during entrance examinations and studies after enrollment, and provides
consultations for this purpose. Those who wish to request accommodations for entrance examinations
should contact the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology Admissions Office (ref.
Section 11 below) by the application deadline. Although requests made after the above deadline will still
be considered, it is recommended that applicants send their requests well in advance as it may not be
possible to provide certain accommodations without sufficient preparation time. (Please refer to the
admission webpage for more details: https://www.i.u-tokyo.ac.jp/edu/entra/entra_e.shtml)
(6) Applicants with foreign nationalities must obtain a visa permitting enrollment at a Japanese graduate school,
as stipulated in the “Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act (Law No. 319, 1951)”, by the time
of enrollment procedures.
(7) Employees of the government, a company, or other corporations wishing to be enrolled at this graduate
11
The document is a translation from the official Japanese version.
In the case of conflict, the Japanese version shall prevail and be conclusive.
school while remaining on the job must submit a letter of approval from the head of the organization at the

to be enrolled as a regular doctoral student at this graduate school. The “head of the organization” can be
anyone who is in a higher position than you. (The exact position does not matter.)
(8) Under some circumstances, application procedures, examination dates, and other details may be subject to
change.
(9) After the application process is complete, no documents or other materials submitted will be returned,
under any circumstances.
(10) After the enrollment procedure is complete, the admission fee will not be refunded under any circumstances.
(11) The University of Tokyo shall use the personal information obtained through the application process only
for the purpose of (1) Selection procedures, (2) Notification of results and (3) Enrollment procedures. For
those who enroll, this personal information and the examination results used for admission selection shall
also be used for (4) Educational Affairs (school registration, attendance, etc.), (5) Student Support
(healthcare, career support, application procedure for tuition exemption and scholarships, use of libraries,
etc.) and (6) the Management of tuition payment.
(12) The examination results used for admission selection may be used in future studies for the improvement of
admission and education systems at the University of Tokyo.
(13) All dates and times stated in this Admission Guide are in Japan Standard Time (JST).
(14) Those who make any false statements in their personal history, application, and/or in any other
accompanying forms, statements or documents may have their admission rescinded even after being
admitted.
(15) In case of an unexpected situation such as natural disasters, please pay attention to the up-to-date
information about entrance examinations posted on the website of this graduate school, etc.
(16) Examination Admission Card and other important notices will be delivered to each applicant via E-mail to
the address stated on the application form. Be sure to configure your E-mail setting so that you can receive
E-mails from the domain u-tokyo.ac.jp and receive notifications when they arrive.

11. Contact Information
If you have any inquiries about entrance examinations, contact us via E-mail instead of calling. We will
reply to your questions during weekdays (except Saturdays, Sundays, and Japanese national holidays) from
9:00 to 17:00 in JST. You should start your application as soon as possible and contact us early if you have
any questions. Note that it can take several days for us to answer your questions. In particular, it may take
a long time to answer your questions during the period just before the Summer Entrance Examinations,
due to the “Obon” holiday season in Japan. During that time, our office may be closed on weekdays, in
addition to Saturdays, Sundays, and national holidays.

The University of Tokyo has established the “The University of Tokyo Security Export Control
Regulations” in accordance with Japan’s “Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act”, and rigorously
implements security export control for potential students before and after their enrollment on the basis of
these regulations. In particular, pre-enrollment screenings are mandatory for all international students and
also for Japanese students in certain circumstances.
Please be aware that applicants who fall under any of the conditions set out in the Act may not receive
permission to enroll at the university or may have their research activities restricted after their enrollment
even if they have passed the entrance examinations.

1. Payment Periods
Tuition payments are made in 6-month amounts twice a year: in May for the first half (April-September) and in November for the second half (October-March).
â»Tuition payments for autumn entrants enrolled at the University in or before September 2018 are as follows:
(1) For the year of entry, payment in November will be for the first seven months (September-March).
(2) For the graduating year, payment in May will be for the last five months (April-August).
(3) For the other years not covered by (1) or (2), payments in May and November will be for six months each.
2. Payment Method (Automatic Bank Account Withdrawal)
• Payments will be deducted automatically from the bank account that you registered using the Tuition Deposit Account Withdrawal Request Form. â»There are no charges for withdrawals from your deposit account.
(To register, click the button below.)
• Tuition fees will be withdrawn from your account on May 27 for the first half and November 27 for the second half (or the next business day if the payment date falls on a non-business day for financial institutions).
• Please be sure to deposit an amount equal to the tuition payment in the relevant account at least one day prior to the withdrawal date.
* You can check which of your accounts is currently registered through the "Payment Status Information" screen of the UTokyo Academic affairs System (UTAS).
(Any application made through the link below during the withdrawal request period [from around the 15th to the end of the month] will be implemented at the beginning of the following month.)

(I) Master’s Program [Summer Entrance Examinations]
1. Outline
Selection will be conducted based on the “AY 2027 Admission Guide: Master’s Program, Graduate
School of Information Science and Technology, The University of Tokyo” (posted on https://www.i.u-
tokyo.ac.jp/edu/entra/entra_e.shtml), and on this admission guide of the Department of Mathematical
Informatics. All important items common to the graduate school, including requirements for eligibility
and application procedures, are listed in the above common guide, so be sure to refer to that document.
This admission guide supplements the above common guide with explanations regarding examination
procedures that are specific to the Department of Mathematical Informatics.
Based on the interdisciplinary nature of the Department of Mathematical Informatics, this department
invites applicants from a wide range of fields, both inside and outside the University of Tokyo, with a
fundamental understanding and knowledge of mathematics, informatics, and physics. Examination
subjects have been selected to ensure that applicants with diverse backgrounds can take examinations
under fair conditions.
2. Declaring preferred faculty advisors, etc.
Declare the following items in the designated fields in the Web application system.
・Preferred faculty advisors: Choose your first to sixth preferences from the pull-down menu in the
field “Your Selection of Lab” on the application system. For the available faculty advisors and their
research areas, consult the list in this Admission Guide. If you have any preferred choices in addition
to the first six choices, fill (list) the information in the following Field 1 for Department-Specific
Information. The choice of preferred faculty advisors does not affect the result.
・ Field 1 for Department-Specific Information: As mentioned above, fill (list) the additional
information on the preferred faculty advisors, if there are any in addition to the first six preferred
choices.
・Field 2 for Department-Specific Information: Declare which language you hope to use in the oral
examination, Japanese or English.
3. Examination Subjects
3.1．Document screening
Document screening will be conducted based on the submitted documents. Regarding the notification
of the screening results, refer to the admission guide of the Graduate School of Information Science
and Technology.
Applicants are required to submit essays at the time of application, following “Document Screening
Assignment (for Master’s Program)” on page 10 of this guide.
3.2．General education subjects
We will conduct a mathematics examination. The examination will be conducted only for applicants
who have passed the document screening. Refer to the admission guide of the Graduate School of
Information Science and Technology for details.
3.3. Foreign language (English)
TOEFL scores will be used to evaluate applicants’ English skills. For details, refer to “Guidelines for
Submission of TOEFL Scores (for AY2027 Entrance Examinations)” which is provided on the

webpage of the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology.
3.4. Specialized subjects and oral examination
The examinations will be conducted only for applicants who have passed the document screening and
taken the written examinations of the general education subjects.
1) Written Examination
For examinations on the specialized subjects, applicants shall choose one subject from among the
following: “Mathematical Informatics” and “Information Physics and Computing.” Please note that
dates, times, and locations differ depending on the subjects.

2) Oral examination
The oral examination will be held online on August 27 (Thursday), 2026 in principle. Examinees will

The oral examination will be conducted only for applicants who have taken the written examinations
for both general education subjects and specialized subjects. Examinees will be notified regarding the
detailed schedule of the oral examination by noon of August 12 (Wednesday), 2026. The schedule
cannot be adjusted. Please take the examination on the date and time specified.
4. Important Notes
4.1. Those who are absent from one of the exams (the general education subjects, the written
examination on the specialized subjects, and the oral examination) will be considered to have
withdrawn from the entrance examination.
4.2. Those who have not submitted their TOEFL scores by the deadline specified by the graduate
school will not be permitted to take the written exams (the general education subjects and the
specialized subjects).
4.3. During the written examinations, applicants can use only writing instruments (pencils or
mechanical pencils; all must be black), pencil sharpeners, erasers, and a clock or watch (only with
timekeeping function). No other instruments can be used.

(II) Doctoral Program [Summer and Winter Entrance Examinations]
1. Outline
Selection will be conducted based on the “AY 2027 Admission Guide: Doctoral Program, Graduate
School of Information Science and Technology, The University of Tokyo” (posted on https://www.i.u-
tokyo.ac.jp/edu/entra/index_e.shtml), and on this admission guide of the Department of Mathematical
Informatics. All important items common to the graduate school, including requirements for eligibility
and application procedures, are listed in the above common guide, so be sure to refer to that document.
This admission guide supplements the above common guide with explanations regarding examination
procedures that are specific to the Department of Mathematical Informatics.
2. Contact before the Submission of the Applications
Applicants are required to meet with their preferred faculty advisor prior to the submission of their
applications.
3. Declaring a preferred faculty advisor, etc.
Declare the following items in the designated fields in the Web application system.
・Preferred faculty advisor: Indicate one in the field “Supervising Professor of your choice” on the
application system.
・Field 1 for the Department-Specific Information: Declare which language you hope to use in the
oral examination, Japanese or English.
4. Documents
Applicants are required to write reports on the following themes and submit them with the application
documents. The reports should be organized so that their answers to each of the questions ((1), (2),
(3)(a)–(e)) are shown to be clear.
Theme:
(1) Summarize your past research achievements and research plans for the Doctoral Program in a
report in Japanese or English, comprising no more than ten A4-sized pages, including formulas,
diagrams, etc. Include a list of your past research achievements at the end of the report. The list
includes academic papers, research presentations, patents, products, and other examples of the
applicant's achievements. In the case of collaborative achievements involving several persons, clearly
indicate the part and the weight of the applicant's contributions for each achievement. Applicants may
use any format appropriate for this report.
(2) Provide an English summary of the above report of about one A4-sized page.
3
This document is an unofficial translation from the official Japanese version.
(3) Provide responses to the following questions regarding the content of the above report in Japanese
or English, comprising no more than two A4-sized pages.
(a) What is the goal of your research?
(b) What are the specific contents of this research and the methods used?
(c) What is the current status of this field of research, in Japan and overseas?
(d) What aspects of this research could be considered new in comparison to past researches in this
field?
(e) How will the results of this research contribute to the field in question?
5. Selection Methods
5.1. Foreign language (English)
・TOEFL scores will be used to evaluate applicants’ English skills. For details, refer to “Guidelines
for Submission of TOEFL Scores (for AY2027 Entrance Examinations)” which is provided on the
webpage of the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology.
・For applicants who have completed or are expected to complete a Master's Program in the University
of Tokyo, the submission is waived.
5.2. Written examination
・ Applicants will take an examination on the specialized subject “Mathematical Informatics.”
Applicants will be required to answer essay-type questions that assess specialized academic skills and
knowledge.
・In the Summer Entrance Examination, the written examination will be held online on August 25
(Tuesday), 2026, in principle. Applicants will be notified of the detailed schedule and the method of
the examination by early August.
・In the Winter Entrance Examination, the written examination will be held online between January
26 (Tuesday) and January 29 (Friday), 2027, in principle. Applicants will be notified of the detailed
schedule and the method of the examination by the middle of January.
・Applicants who have completed or are expected to complete a Master's Program of the University
of Tokyo may be exempted from the specialized subject written examination. The decision regarding
the exemption will be notified to the applicants around mid-July for the summer entrance examination
and around late December for the winter entrance examination.
5.3. Oral examination
・Applicants will be required to answer questions on the research plan and other aspects of the
submitted documents. Applicants should prepare presentation slides summarizing the descriptions on
your past research achievements and future research plans for the Doctoral Program in the submitted
documents.
・In the Summer Entrance Examination, the oral examination will be held online between August 25
(Tuesday) and August 26 (Wednesday), 2026, in principle. Applicants will be notified of the detailed
schedule and the method of the examination by early August.
・In the Winter Entrance Examination, the oral examination will be held online between January 27
(Wednesday) and January 29 (Friday), 2027, in principle. Applicants will be notified regarding the
detailed schedule and the method of the examination by the middle of January.

application system.
・Field 1 for the Department-Specific Information: Declare which language you hope to use in the
oral examination, Japanese or English.
4. Documents
Applicants are required to prepare for the following five items regarding applicants' research and work
achievements in a field related to Mathematical Informatics.
(1) List of achievements
Provide a list of academic papers, research presentations, patents, products, and other examples of the
applicant's achievements. In the case of collaborative achievements involving several persons, clearly
indicate the part and the weight of the applicant's contributions.
(2) Outline of main achievements
Select three or fewer main achievements from the above list, and provide an outline of these
achievements.
(3) Research plan
Provide a detailed description of the applicant's plan for research to be conducted in the Doctoral
Program.
5
This document is an unofficial translation from the official Japanese version.
(4) Materials related to main achievements
These materials may include reprints (or copies) of academic papers, detailed descriptions of patents,
or product pamphlets.
(5) Recommendation letters

provide separate evaluations of those achievements. Use the Word file “Recommendation letters
(Doctoral Program [Special Selection for Professionals])” on the department webpage and submit the
file following the instructions on the department webpage and on the webpage of the Graduate School
of Information Science and Technology.
Note: Items (2) and (3) should be combined in about ten A4-sized pages.

2. Examination locations
The University of Tokyo (7-3-1 Hongo, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo)
Refer to the map on page 9.
By subway:
Marunouchi Line / Oedo Line: Get off at Hongo Sanchome Station
Chiyoda Line: Get off at Nezu Station
Namboku Line: Get off at Todai Mae Station
Mita Line: Get off at Kasuga Station
By Bus:
Take Toei Bus No. 43 or 51 to “Todai Seimon Mae” (Main Gate of The University of Tokyo),
or Toei School Bus No. 1 or 7 to “Todai Konai” (Campus of The University of Tokyo).
Examinees should be in the designated examination room no later than 15 minutes before the start of
the examination. In case of being late, the examinee should immediately contact an examination
administrator.
3. What to bring
(1) Paper-based Examination Admission Card (printed on A4-sized paper)
(2) Be sure to bring black pencils (or mechanical pencil), erasers, pencil sharpeners (desktop types are
not acceptable) if you are using black pencils, and a clock or watch (only with time-keeping function).
Caution: During the examination time, all mobile phones must be turned off and must not be worn.
4. Items to keep in mind during examinations
(1) Examinees will not be allowed to leave the examination room after the start of the examination,
even after finishing writing answers or even when you abandon the examination.
(2) Examinees will not be allowed, in principle, to leave their seats even temporarily. Call the proctor
in case feeling sick or needing to go to the bathroom during the examination time.
(3) Examination admission cards must be placed on the desks throughout the examination time.
(4) Write your examinee’s number on all answer sheets. It is not allowed to write your name. Write
your answer on each designated sheet. If there is not enough space, you may write on the back of the
answer sheet.
(5) Examinees are not allowed to take answer sheets and question booklets out of the examination
room.
